semantics.note: Keeps the 'wishes to grow' antecedent, the mid-2025 horizon, and the firm requirements of more money at a higher valuation. The dollar figures stay hedged with 'likely' and are not scored as thresholds.

contract.note: Using June 30 for 'middle of 2025' and requiring an executed closing is an ordinary reading. The contract scores whether the financing happened, not whether it was strictly necessary, and says so. That is fair to the forecast as written.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure from Jan 2025 on the Stargate buildout. It shows intent to expand, so the antecedent is met. Company statement about itself.

SoftBank filing, available July 2025, before the evaluation date. It records a completed $10B first closing on Apr 15, 2025 at a $260B pre-money valuation. That is more money and a higher valuation than the baseline, before the deadline.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent was met: Stargate shows OpenAI planned to expand. By April 15, 2025 OpenAI had closed a $10B round at a $260B pre-money valuation. That beats the Oct 2024 round of $6.6B at $157B and comes before the mid-2025 deadline, which has now passed. Only the first tranche had closed, but that is enough under the contract. The figures even match the hedged estimates.

contract.note: Using Q3 2024 and reading the words as losses plus reliance on outside financing is ordinary and fair. The quarter is the evaluator's choice, as the contract flags.

OpenAI's own disclosure of a $6.6B raise. It shows financing was available but says nothing on whether operations paid for themselves in the quarter.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs realized results, cash flow, and liquidity for Jul–Sep 2024. The packet has only a full-year loss projection and a fundraising announcement. Both point toward losses, but neither settles the target quarter, and the packet admits no quarterly results were found.

Epoch AI piece published Oct 2025, before the evaluation date. Gives company-wide 2024 inference cost estimates (~$1.8B) and does not isolate free-tier cost. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The subscriber part (~10M payers) is supported. Nothing in the packet isolates what the free tier cost during the target period, and company-wide inference figures can't stand in for it. The central 'burns billions' claim is therefore unsettled.

Gives the $11.6B 2025 target but no breakdown by product.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows ChatGPT was about 73% of projected 2024 revenue and the 2025 target. It has no Plus-specific projections and no breakdown of how much each product had to contribute. That is not enough to establish or refute near-total dependence on Plus growth.
